title: How do you build a training matrix for a government agency?
seoTitle: Training matrix for a government agency
description: Build a government agency training matrix: security, ethics, records, privacy, CUI and integrity duties by position, with clocks and audit evidence.
shortAnswer: A government agency training matrix is built by listing the positions that public sector rules single out, such as ethics filers, privileged system users, records custodians, CUI handlers, security staff and report handlers, against the security, ethics, records, privacy and integrity obligations of the agency's own government. Each cell records the clock the rule sets, which is often fixed in public sector rules, the trigger, and the evidence that inspectors general, auditors or central agencies will test.
keyTakeaways: Public sector rules fix intervals more often than private sector ones: annual security awareness, annual ethics training for filers, annual records refreshers and biennial CUI training are all written into rule text.
Contractors, students, guest researchers and visitors are often in scope alongside employees, so the matrix must include non-employee rows.
Several rules require training before system access or within a set number of days of appointment, so onboarding triggers matter as much as anniversaries.
Central reporting drives evidence: FISMA independent evaluations, PSPF annual reports to ministers and OGE confirmations to the agency ethics official all draw on matrix data.
As at November 2026, new PSPF foreign interference content, an ISM control on synthetic impersonation and Japan's amended Whistleblower Protection Act all change agency rows.

sections.heading: What is different about a training matrix in the public sector?

blocks.text: Government training rules are usually issued by central agencies for the whole public service, so they tend to name fixed intervals, set content lists and require reporting upward. A private company often has to justify its own refresh cycle; an agency more often has to prove that it met a cycle someone else set, for every person, including contractors.

That shifts the work from choosing frequencies to managing triggers and populations. The structure from [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) still holds, but the agency version needs columns for the access event that starts each clock, for clearance or filer status, and for the central report each row feeds. Starting from an [obligations to training map](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations) keeps each of those columns tied to the rule that created it.

sections.heading: Which agency positions need their own rows?

blocks.text: Give a row to every position a central rule names, then keep one baseline row for all personnel. Most agencies end up with the positions below.

sections.heading: Which training obligations apply to agencies in each government?

blocks.text: Each government sets its own public sector rules, so the columns come from the regulation pages for the agency's jurisdiction. The summaries below draw only on those pages.

items: **United States, security.** The Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA), at 44 U.S.C. 3554(b)(4), requires security awareness training for personnel, including contractors and other system users. The Office of Personnel Management's rule at 5 CFR 930.301(a)(1) says all users must be exposed to security awareness materials at least annually, and 930.301(b) requires awareness material for new employees before system access ([federal cybersecurity awareness](/regulations/federal-employee-cybersecurity-awareness-training)). NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1 (September 2024) gives federal guidance for running security and privacy awareness and training as one program, with measurements that must go beyond simply achieving compliance ([NIST SP 800-50](/regulations/nist-sp-800-50-security-awareness-training)).

**United States, ethics.** Under 5 CFR Part 2638, Subpart C, from the Office of Government Ethics (OGE), new employees complete interactive initial ethics training within 3 months of appointment, and filers, contracting officers and some other employees complete at least 1 hour of annual training before the end of each calendar year ([federal ethics training](/regulations/us-federal-ethics-training-requirements)).

**United States, records and CUI.** 36 CFR 1220.34(f) requires training for all agency personnel on records management responsibilities, and NARA Bulletin 2017-01 sets initial training within 60 days and an annual refresher ([NARA records management](/regulations/nara-records-management-training-requirements)). 32 CFR 2002.30(c) requires Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) training when employees start and at least once every two years; DoD Instruction 5200.48 requires initial and annual refresher training for DoD personnel ([CUI training](/regulations/cui-training-requirements)).

**Australia (Commonwealth).** The Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2026 requires non-corporate Commonwealth entities to provide security awareness training at engagement and annually (Requirement 0024) and targeted training for specialist or high-risk positions (Requirement 0025) ([PSPF](/regulations/pspf-security-awareness-training)). The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual (ISM) sets annual awareness training (ISM-0252), tailored annual training for privileged users (ISM-1565) and a training register (ISM-2022) ([ISM](/regulations/ism-cyber-security-awareness-training)). The agencies' privacy code requires privacy training at induction and annually for staff with access to personal information ([Privacy Act](/regulations/privacy-act-staff-training-requirements)).

**European Union and Portugal.** NIS2 covers public administration among its sectors; Article 20(2) requires management body members to follow cybersecurity training and Article 21(2)(g) lists cybersecurity training among the minimum measures ([NIS2](/regulations/nis2-management-body-training)). The Whistleblower Directive covers public sector entities, subject to national exemptions for small municipalities ([EU Whistleblower Directive](/regulations/eu-whistleblower-directive-obligations)). In Portugal, the General Regime for the Prevention of Corruption (RGPC) reaches state, regional, local and public enterprise bodies with 50 or more workers, and Article 9 requires training for all managers and workers calibrated to risk exposure ([Portugal anti-corruption regime](/regulations/portugal-anti-corruption-regime-training)).

**Japan.** Consumer Affairs Agency Guidelines treat national and local government bodies as business operators under the Whistleblower Protection Act, and the national government guideline, last revised 29 May 2026, asks each administrative body to make the Act and its reporting system fully known to all staff through periodic training or briefings ([Japan Whistleblower Protection Act](/regulations/japan-whistleblower-protection-act-training)).

**United Arab Emirates.** The Information Assurance Regulation from the Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA) is mandatory for government entities; controls M3.2.1 and M3.3.1 on the awareness program and training needs are Always Applicable and cannot be excluded through risk assessment ([UAE Information Assurance](/regulations/uae-information-assurance-awareness-training)).

sections.heading: Which start events and intervals should an agency matrix track?

blocks.text: Track the start event first, because many public sector rules attach a deadline to an access grant, an appointment or a departure. Then layer the refresh interval on top.

items: **Before access.** 5 CFR 930.301(b) requires awareness material before new employees get system access, and OMB Circular A-130 calls for role-based training before authorizing access or performing assigned duties. Wire these rows to account provisioning, not to the HR start date.

**Within a number of days.** OGE initial ethics training is due within 3 months of appointment; NARA records training within 60 days of employment; written notice to new supervisors within 1 year of a first supervisory appointment; a live briefing for Senate-confirmed appointees within 15 days.

**Fixed refresh intervals.** Security awareness at least annually (OPM, PSPF, ISM); ethics for filers each calendar year; records annually; CUI at least every two years under Part 2002, or annually for DoD under DoDI 5200.48; privacy annually for Australian agency staff with access to personal information.

**Risk-based intervals.** Portugal's RGPC requires frequency to reflect each person's exposure to identified corruption risks, and MENAC guidance suggests an annual training needs survey. 5 CFR 930.301(c) leaves refresher frequency for role training to the agency. Document these choices; see [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).
**Event triggers.** Significant system changes and entry into a new position (930.301(d)), departures of senior officials, and changes of administration all restart rows.

sections.heading: What evidence do inspectors general and central agencies expect?

blocks.text: They expect evidence that feeds a formal report, so the matrix should be able to produce completion by position, by population and by deadline. Central reporting is built into most of these rules.

items: **Independent evaluation.** 44 U.S.C. 3555 requires an annual independent evaluation of agency security programs by the Inspector General or an independent external auditor.

**Knowledge testing.** OMB Circular A-130 Appendix I requires agencies to test users' knowledge, and OGE defines interactive training so that the action required may not be limited to advancing between sections.

**Upward confirmations.** In agencies with 1,000 or more employees, delegated offices submit ethics training procedures and confirmation to the Designated Agency Ethics Official by January 15 each year. PSPF Accountable Authorities report compliance annually to their minister and to Home Affairs. DoDI 5200.48 requires CUI training documentation maintained for audit and annual reporting of completion data.

**Registers and records.** ISM-2022 requires a training register. The UAE IA Regulation control M3.2.1 requires records of education, training, skills, experience and qualifications, and evaluation of training effectiveness.

**Program evaluation.** 36 CFR 1220.34(j) requires formal evaluations of records management programs, which will include training coverage. The guide on [evidencing training effectiveness to a regulator](/guides/how-to-evidence-training-effectiveness-to-a-regulator) covers presenting this.

**No excuse for non-delivery.** 5 CFR 2638.301 says an agency's failure to deliver ethics training does not exempt any employee from ethics requirements, which is a reason to track overdue rows by person.

sections.heading: Which public sector training rules are changing in 2026 and 2027?

blocks.text: Several agency rows have changed during 2026 or will change shortly. As at November 2026, the regulation pages record these dates:

items: **1 July 2026, Australia:** PSPF Release 2026 took effect, with Requirement 0219 adding foreign interference, espionage, cultivation and exploitation by foreign powers to awareness training.
**September 2026, Australia:** the ISM September 2026 release added ISM-2126 on verifying requests that could be synthetic voice or video, and amended ISM-1565 without changing its intent.

**1 December 2026, Japan:** the amended Whistleblower Protection Act takes effect, adding an express duty to inform workers, freelancer coverage and offenses for dismissing or disciplining national public servants because of a report. Amended Guidelines apply from the same date.
**10 December 2026, Australia:** automated decision making transparency obligations under the Privacy Act commence, which affects privacy training for staff involved in those decisions.
**Already in force, Portugal:** Decree-Law 125/2025 transposing NIS2 entered into force on 3 April 2026, with management bodies required to ensure regular training.

blocks.title: Proposed, not yet law
blocks.text: The FAR Controlled Unclassified Information proposed rule of 15 January 2025, which would bar contractor employees from handling CUI until trained, had not been finalized as at November 2026. Australia's exposure draft Privacy Amendment (Personal Data Protection) Bill 2026 and the European Commission's January 2026 proposal for targeted NIS2 amendments are also pending.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each public sector obligation with its source, the position and start event it attaches to, and the learning outcome and assessment that satisfy it, so a new PSPF requirement or a revised OGE rule flags the affected positions and content. See [government and defense](/industries/government-defence).

faqs.q: Can one annual course satisfy security awareness and CUI training?
faqs.a: Often, if the content covers both and the record shows it. DoDI 5200.48 has the DoD CIO integrate CUI training into initial and annual cybersecurity awareness training. Map the combined course to each rule's content list, such as the six areas in 32 CFR 2002.30(b), so each obligation can be evidenced separately.

faqs.q: Do contractors belong in an agency training matrix?
faqs.a: Yes. 5 CFR 930.301 defines users to include contractors, students, guest researchers and visitors, PSPF Requirement 0024 covers contractors, and NARA Bulletin 2017-01 covers contractors and volunteers who handle federal records. CUI training reaches contractors through contract clauses rather than Part 2002 directly.

faqs.q: Should a state or local agency use federal or Commonwealth rules?
faqs.a: Only where they apply. The ISM, for example, is mandatory for Commonwealth entities through the PSPF and adopted voluntarily by many state, territory and local bodies. Record whether each row is mandatory or adopted so auditors know which standard is being tested.

faqs.q: What happens if an employee misses initial ethics training?
faqs.a: The employee is still bound by the ethics rules. 5 CFR 2638.301 states that an agency's failure to deliver training does not exempt any employee. The matrix should flag the overdue row to the ethics office and the supervisor well before the 3 month deadline.
